summary: Opaque native addon exposes browser-credential-harvest and host-enumeration capabilities
details: This platform-specific sub-package ships only a ~10 MB Linux x64 napi-rs.node addon as `main` with a minimal README that does not describe the addon's function. String extraction from the binary reveals Chromium-login harvest strings ('Found login for'), embedded SQLite with authenticated-user support (SQLITE_AUTH_USER), a Rust HTTP/TLS stack (ureq, rustls), host-enumeration primitives (getifaddrs, gethostname, reads of /dev/disk/by-id and /etc/lsb-release, a network_adapters enumerator), and process-spawning primitives (posix_spawnp, execvp). No install lifecycle hooks are declared, so the capabilities do not fire on `npm install` alone; they are reachable through the parent JS wrapper `new-native-tools` that loads this addon via napi_register_module_v1. The combination of browser-login database reading, host fingerprinting, and an in-binary HTTP client inside an undocumented native addon with a browser-release-versioned name is the shape of a credential-stealer native component, not of a general-purpose developer tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
